Title: Strike: Combat Ends ruling - unbalancing and illogical?

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
The Design Team ruled (11/9/94) that if the acting minion in a combat
plays a strike: combat ends, then the blocking minion gets no strike,
not even the opportunity to play a strike card. The precludes even
playing another strike: combat ends.

Why? Nowhere in the rules does it suggest that one strike could remove the
remainder of the Choose strike phase, even before the chosen strike resolves.

Section 15.3:
Combat Ends: Considered a strike, this ends combat immediately (before
any damage is dealt or any strike's effects take place). Note that combat
ends is not affected by Dodge and even cancels strikes with first strike.

The effect of the above rule is: *when the strike resolves* combat is over,
cancelling any effects (already resolved) of a first strike, and nullifying
the (pending) effects of the opposing minion's strike.

Now, this usually doen't matter either way. But, when you are up against
a "Majestic Bleed" deck, the acting minion suddenly has a big advantage.

Since the "... this vampire may pay 1 to untap" clause of majesty is not part
of the strike (IMHO), both minions should be capable of playing superior
Majesties (and/or Earth Melds) to untap. This would remain true to the
original (and the updated) rules, while mantaining some small measure
of balance for the blocking minion (who should usually have the advantage).

This is not MtG, there are no interrupt effects. I don't know why Majesty
would be an exception.

L. Scott

Probably to enable Combat Ends vs. a Rotschrecking Gangrel. Or maybe they
just didn't think about it. It might have been because of resolution
problems if the opponent First Strikes.

A *MAJOR* problem.

Incidentally, I think that "combat ends" is generally too good a card.
It's enormously superior to a dodge and always available at normal skill.
